title: Fppf local models for the diagonal of an etale quotient sheaf
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U,R$ be $S$-schemes, and let $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be a monomorphism identifying $R(W)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(W)$ for every $S$-scheme $W$. Suppose $s,t$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. On the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], let $F$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $W\mapsto U(W)/R(W)$, and let $q:h_U\to F$ be the canonical map, where $h_Z(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(W,Z)$. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume $j$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. For every $S$-scheme $T$ and two maps $a_1,a_2:h_T\to F$, let $H=h_T\times_{(a_1,a_2),F\times F,\Delta}F$, viewed as a presheaf on $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$. This is a sheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; on a test scheme $W\to T$ its set of sections is a singleton if $a_1|_W=a_2|_W$ and empty otherwise. There exist a common fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and maps $u_i,v_i:T_i\to U$ with $q(u_i)=a_1|_{T_i}$ and $q(v_i)=a_2|_{T_i}$, together with natural identifications $H|_{T_i}\simeq h_{Y_i}$, where $Y_i=T_i\times_{(u_i,v_i),U\times_SU,j}R$. Every $Y_i\to T_i$ is separated and locally quasi-finite.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, third representability step, cartesian square and local model; simultaneous local lifts are obtained directly from sheafification on a common fppf refinement.

proof.text: For a test scheme $W\to T$, an element of the displayed presheaf fibre product is an $x\in F(W)$ satisfying $x=a_1|_W=a_2|_W$. Thus $H(W)$ is a singleton exactly when the two sections agree, and empty otherwise. This presheaf is a sheaf: a matching family on a covering exists exactly when the two sections agree on every covering member; the uniqueness part of the sheaf condition for $F$ then makes them agree on $W$. The resulting unique element of $H(W)$ glues the family. This also handles an empty covering, since a sheaf has exactly one section on any object admitting an empty cover.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, third step, definition of the diagonal fibre; sectionwise sheaf-condition verification.

proof.text: Let P be the presheaf coequalizer, π:h_U→P, and q=π≫η. The universal property hη implies that η is locally surjective, without constructing sheafification in a larger universe: the locally generated image R=(range η).sheafify is a subsheaf of F; factor η through R by hη, and use uniqueness to show that the resulting F→R splits its inclusion. Thus every F-section is locally in the image of η. The components of π are epimorphisms of types, hence surjective, so q is locally surjective. For the two sections corresponding by Yoneda to a₁ and a₂, intersect their covering image sieves. The precoverage criterion supplies one fppf covering presieve inside this intersection. Present it as an indexed family, choose the two preimages on every member, and translate their section equalities into equalities of natural transformations by Yoneda. The forgetful slice functor identifies this with the required fppf covering of the underlying scheme.

source.place: Tags 00WB and 00WK, local generation of sheafification; the image-subsheaf proof of local surjectivity works directly with the given universal property. Tag 00VH and the covering-sieve criterion give the common refinement.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair] apply to the given monomorphism $j$ and the sectionwise equivalence relation. Consequently, for every $W$ and $b,c:W\to U$, equality $q(b)=q(c)$ is equivalent to the existence of a unique $r:W\to R$ with $s r=b$ and $t r=c$: evaluate its canonical isomorphism $h_R\simeq h_U\times_Fh_U$ on $W$. This uses the isomorphism clause, not just local existence of relation witnesses.

source.place: Tag 045Y, lemma-quotient-pre-equivalence, with the monomorphic equivalence-relation kernel-pair statement; Tag 0265 cartesian square.

proof.text: Form $Y_i=T_i\times_{(u_i,v_i),U\times_SU,j}R$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. On a test map $w:W\to T_i$, its relative functor of points consists of $r:W\to R$ with $s r=u_iw$ and $t r=v_iw$, by the fibre-product universal property. Step 3 identifies this set with the singleton witnessing $q(u_iw)=q(v_iw)$, or with the empty set if equality fails. By the lifting equalities of step 2 this is exactly $H(W)$ from step 1. Send a relation witness to this equality; conversely recover the unique witness from step 3. These assignments are inverse. Precomposition sends $r$ to its composite with the test morphism, so uniqueness proves that the inverse also commutes with restriction. Hence this is the required natural identification $H|_{T_i}\simeq h_{Y_i}$ on the big fppf site over $T_i$.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, third step, cartesian square and cube, evaluated on test schemes.

proof.text: The structure morphism Y_i→T_i is the first projection of the specified pullback of j. Separatedness is supplied by Mathlib's base-change instance. For local quasi-finiteness, use the proved Scheme.Hom.isLocallyQuasiFinite_iff comparison API for [pqf-def-quasifinite] to convert the Stacks predicate on j into Mathlib LocallyQuasiFinite and LocallyOfFiniteType. Both properties are stable under base change by Mathlib instances, including for the first projection. Convert their conjunction back by the same comparison. This avoids transporting the second-projection interface of lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change across the pullback symmetry. No extra hypotheses are introduced.

lean.statement: theorem quotient_diagonal_fppf_local_models {S : Scheme.{u}} {R U : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ U) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] (hrel : ∀ W : Over S, Equivalence (fun b c : W ⟶ U ↦ ∃ r : W ⟶ R, r ≫ s = b ∧ r ≫ t = c)) [Etale s.left] [Etale t.left] (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ F.obj) (hη : ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun g : F.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ g)) [IsSeparated (prod.lift s t).left] (hj : Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (prod.lift s t).left) (T : Over S) (a₁ a₂ : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj) : Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over T.left) (quotientDiagonalFibre T F a₁ a₂) ∧ (∀ W : Over T.left, Subsingleton ((quotientDiagonalFibre T F a₁ a₂).obj (op W)) ∧ (Nonempty ((quotientDiagonalFibre T F a₁ a₂).obj (op W)) ↔ a₁.app (op ((Over.map T.hom).obj W)) (Over.homMk W.hom) = a₂.app (op ((Over.map T.hom).obj W)) (Over.homMk W.hom))) ∧ ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (Tᵢ : I → Over S) (f : ∀ i, Tᵢ i ⟶ T) (uᵢ vᵢ : ∀ i, Tᵢ i ⟶ U), Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ (Tᵢ i).left) (fun i ↦ (f i).left) ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T.left ∧ (∀ i, yoneda.map (uᵢ i) ≫ (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η) = yoneda.map (f i) ≫ a₁) ∧ (∀ i, yoneda.map (vᵢ i) ≫ (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η) = yoneda.map (f i) ≫ a₂) ∧ (∀ i, Nonempty ((Over.map (f i).left).op ⋙ quotientDiagonalFibre T F a₁ a₂ ≅ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (pullback.fst (prod.lift (uᵢ i) (vᵢ i)).left (prod.lift s t).left)))) ∧ (∀ i, IsSeparated (pullback.fst (prod.lift (uᵢ i) (vᵢ i)).left (prod.lift s t).left) ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (pullback.fst (prod.lift (uᵢ i) (vᵢ i)).left (prod.lift s t).left))
